summary: Concept-stage gate over PRD.md (653 lines, commit 808558c, branch build-brief-run2), reviewed against its own source brief at /Users/m5/Downloads/dev-harness-BUILD-BRIEF_2.md. Decision is GO. The three things a concept gate exists to judge are all real here: the done-state is stated as seven metrics with thresholds and a named measuring command, with M5's threshold left explicitly open rather than faked; the out-of-scope list carries nine items each with its reason; and the falsification pass in section 7 changed four requirements and accepted two as weak on the record instead of gesturing at risk. I did not take the document's evidence on trust. Six load-bearing claims were re-derived in this context from the tree directly and every one held: the three named guards are absent from bollard/; store.py reads MI 4.78 grade C, max_cc 32, SLOC 1443; store.py churn is 1 against a 9-commit tree, so hotspot_signal reduces to max_cc exactly as R18 states; atlas/ingest/audit.py writes payload_json verbatim with no scrub; git ls-files returns zero for all three measurement scripts; and an independent fourth search over /Users/m5/dev for layered_command_guard.py and its four class names returns only PRD.md itself. GO rather than HOLD on the R14/R15 provenance question, deliberately. That question is already quarantined correctly - the PRD forbids R14/R15 entering a backlog or being sized until the operator settles it - so it is a drawn scope boundary, not a leak. It is also unresolvable by any action the architecture stage could take, which makes a Hold on it an open-ended Hold of the kind this skill's section 6 forbids, and it would stall roughly eighteen requirements that do not depend on it. It travels forward as an operator question with a default attached, per condition C1. One finding of my own, not inherited: section 8 records R0 as 'Closed by Run 1', and the evidence behind that closure does not hold up. This finding has been revised twice as better evidence arrived; revision 3 is the accurate statement and supersedes both earlier ones. Revision 1 said no dev-harness-scoped run existed - wrong, one does. Revision 2 said its 1.16x reading contradicted the brief's 0.96x, framed as two disagreeing measurements - also wrong, and wrong in a way that understated the real problem. There are at least four readings of this ratio on record: 0.96x and 1.1x from two dev-harness-7f runs around 22:3x-22:44 (terminal only, never written to a file), 1.16x from the 23:00:53 scoped run surviving at /Users/m5/dev/investigation/dev-harness-token-bloat-diagnostic-scoped-20260901.txt, and 0.64x in the m5-dev--scoped JSON that overwrote the raw output at 23:03:58. They are not competing measurements of one quantity. They are one unstable metric read at four moments, and the instability has an open ticket already: DEVH-5 records that day_over_day compares against a fixed historical day_one, so the ratio moves with whatever scope and session growth happen to be in the window. The current JSON demonstrates it - day_one is 2026-08-06, while dev-harness transcripts only reach back to Aug 23, so its day_one belongs to another project entirely. The actual defect in section 8 is therefore sharper than a disagreement: R0 was closed on a single favorable reading of a metric that this project's own open bug says is not stable enough to close anything on. DEVH-4 and DEVH-5 both remain open. Two attribution points, recorded because this package is the durable record. The 23:00 scoped file was NOT produced by dev-harness-7f - that was this session's inference from '7f ran R0', never something any peer stated, and 7f corrected it; its provenance is unestablished and nothing here should imply otherwise. And DEVH-3, open when this gate was first rendered, was transitioned to closed at 2026-09-02T09:32:04Z with a comment recording the retraction and the attribution fix, which resolves that leg of C2. Still no bearing on the gate: R0 is out of this PRD's scope and no R1-R24 requirement rests on it. This package was written by a session that did not author the PRD, did not author the brief, and holds none of the reasoning that produced either. Recorded explicitly because concept_gate.py's own docstring names the unenforceability of that separation as a known open limitation - the hook cannot check it, so the claim belongs on the record instead.

r0_metric_instability_evidence.objection_tested: Tenfold spread alone is attackable as small-sample noise, and partly is: the three lowest ratios sit on the three thinnest days - 0.25x on 47 turns, 0.5x on 42, 0.64x on 106. A sceptic is right to discount those. The spread argument should not be leaned on in that form.
r0_metric_instability_evidence.robust_form: Restrict to days with >=1000 turns (n=9): 2.09, 2.11, 1.82, 1.25, 1.93, 2.14, 1.96, 1.78, 1.78. Median about 1.93. Every well-sampled day sits above the 1.1 target and not one is near parity. The instability finding survives the noise objection in this form, where the raw spread does not.
r0_metric_instability_evidence.mechanism_demonstrated: The headline latest_vs_day_one_ratio of 0.64 comes from 2026-09-01, a 106-turn partial day. So the headline is a two-point comparison between two arbitrary days, either of which may be thin. That is DEVH-5's defect shown working, not merely asserted, and it is why no single reading of this ratio - 0.96x, 1.1x, 1.16x or 0.64x - can close anything.
r0_metric_instability_evidence.do_not_quote: 0.64x must never be cited as reassurance. It is a thin-day artifact on a cross-project scope, not a dev-harness measurement.
r0_metric_instability_evidence.confidence: High on the arithmetic, read directly from the JSON. Medium on the >=1000-turn cut being the right subset - that is this session's analysis choice, defensible but not independently validated. No causal claim is made about why per-turn tokens are higher on well-sampled days; workload change and metric defect both remain live explanations.
